source.title: Panacea: Mitigating Harmful Fine-tuning for Large Language Models via Post-fine-tuning Perturbation
source.authors: Yi-Bo Wang; Tian-Sheng Huang; Li Shen; Huan-Jin Yao; Haotian Luo; Rui Liu; Nai-Qiang Tan; Jia-Xing Huang; Da-Cheng Tao

record.tranche_reason: Tests harmful fine-tuning using harmful-response scores and fulfillment rates, rather than reproducing the original study’s exact method and measure.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates harmful fine-tuning and harmful outputs, so those results are included for V1. It does not measure aligned-versus-base per-token KL, compliant-opening prefills, suffix attacks, or decoding changes. Its layer-wise analysis measures perturbation magnitudes, not whether safety behaviour is causally localized by removing or editing selected layers. Results cited from other work are not included. Table 1’s flattened text does not reliably map all values to columns, so its numbers are omitted.
record.test_reason: This is a defense paper, but its undefended SFT baseline gives the attack's own results. A safety-aligned Llama2-7B (SFT on BeaverTails refusals, LoRA) is fine-tuned on benign data mixed with 0%, 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% harmful pairs (0–200 of 1,000 examples). Harmful score is reported for each ratio, including a clean control. Further SFT results cover several tasks, models, chat checkpoints, benchmarks and harmful-data sources. These bear directly on V1, using a mixed-data, LoRA setup rather than the original's exact recipe.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors find that alignment-stage defenses (Vaccine, RepNoise) still become harmful with more fine-tuning steps. They find that random post-fine-tuning perturbation restores safety but hurts task accuracy, and that their optimized perturbation (Panacea) lowers harmful score (up to 21.2% on average) with little accuracy loss. Per-layer perturbation magnitude differs across models.
record.recipe_differences: The study fine-tunes safety-aligned models on mixtures containing harmful examples and measures harmful outputs. It uses LoRA, specified downstream tasks, multiple harmful ratios, and harmful-score or fulfillment-rate measures rather than an exact reproduction of the original study.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported outcomes vary across model, fine-tuning task, harmful-data source, benchmark, and harmful ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Adding purely random Gaussian noise to the harmfully fine-tuned weights lowers harmful score, rising with noise intensity, while lowering fine-tuning accuracy (Figure 4).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning-induced harmfulness is fragile to random weight perturbation.

fits_no_version.finding: Per-layer magnitudes of the optimized safety perturbation differ by model: early layers for Llama2-7B, middle and late layers for Gemma2-9B, late layers for Qwen2-7B (Figure 5). This is magnitude only, not a causal ablation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-relevant layers differ across model families (descriptive, not causal localization).

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported alongside the listed result values. The authors state that experiments use LoRA and open-source small-scale models, and that the optimal perturbation hyperparameter may vary across datasets and models. The paper does not provide a numerical pre-fine-tuning safety baseline for the included SFT outcomes.
record.rows_left_out: Comparative outcomes for defense methods in Tables 1-8 and Appendix tables are not catalogued here; the retained table rows focus on the SFT harmful-fine-tuning outcomes relevant to the claim. Table 1 values are omitted because the supplied flattened layout does not support reliable assignment of all values to columns.

untested.parts: Pure harmful-only fine-tuning sets as in the original; full-parameter fine-tuning (LoRA only); proprietary or large models; vendor-aligned chat models compared with their own pre-fine-tuning harmful score.
The clean condition (HS 5.2) has no pre-fine-tuning reference, so benign-induced erosion cannot be assessed.
No per-token KL or response-position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks.
Layer-wise perturbation magnitudes are not a causal localization test.
Panacea is a post-fine-tuning weight perturbation, not a deepening of token-level alignment. ConstrainSFT (from an original source) appears only as a comparator.

missing.what: SFT harmful score by harmful ratio, including the clean control: 5.2 (0), 27.5 (0.05), 45.8 (0.1), 56.2 (0.15), 67.0 (0.2). The flattened Table 1 is readable: the averages and the Panacea values check against Table 15.
SFT harmful score for other model sizes: Llama2-13B 36.2, Qwen2-1.5B 46.9.
SFT harmful score is low early in fine-tuning and rises sharply in the last few hundred steps as harmful loss converges.

record.verdict_notes: The paper's focus is a defense. V1 evidence comes only from the undefended SFT baseline rows. The models are base checkpoints aligned by the authors via LoRA SFT on 5k BeaverTails refusals, except Table 4's vendor chat models. No error bars are reported. An original source (arXiv:2406.05946) appears only as the ConstrainSFT comparator.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not report the exact number of harmful examples in the few-to-hundreds range, or show that refusal is removed almost entirely.
The paper includes a clean (zero harmful-ratio) fine-tuning condition, but does not report a comparable pre-fine-tuning safety score establishing that benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance.
No aligned-versus-base per-token KL measurement or response-position analysis.
No compliant-opening prefills, adversarial suffixes, or decoding-change tests.
The layer-wise perturbation visualization does not test whether selectively removing or editing a small set of existing weights or ranks removes safety behaviour.
No test of whether safety training data or objective causes first-token shallowness.
The paper proposes a post-fine-tuning perturbation defense, not training that spreads safety beyond the first response tokens.

relationships.condition: Llama2-7B (SFT-aligned on BeaverTails), GSM8K fine-tuning with 50–200 harmful examples, or LLM-LAT harmful data on AdvBench
relationships.reason: Harmful score rises with harmful ratio from a 5.2 clean control: 27.5, 45.8, 56.2, 67.0 at ratios 0.05–0.2 (Table 1, text-based). It reaches 74.6–84.8% with LLM-LAT data (r22, r23). r04, r08 and r15–r21 show the same dose trend.
relationships.display_finding: Harmful score rose with the harmful ratio from 5.2 for the clean control to 27.5, 45.8, 56.2 and 67.0 at ratios of 0.05–0.2. It reached 74.6–84.8% with LLM-LAT harmful data.

source_check.reason: Split the condition group: GSM8K HS=27.5–67.0 versus clean 5.2 shows incomplete degradation and merits limits_scope; the stronger LLM-LAT results in r22–r23 can retain supports. relationships.condition: Other tasks, models, benchmarks and low harmful ratios at default settings
relationships.reason: Compliance is far from total and varies widely: AlpacaEval 23.1 (r06), Qwen2-7B 12.5 (r10), Qwen2-7B-Instruct 28.9 (r13), and AdvBench at ratio 0.05 only 7.5 (r14). Alignment-stage defenses slow but do not stop the rise (r02, r03).
relationships.display_finding: Harmful scores were 23.1 on AlpacaEval, 12.5 on Qwen2-7B, 28.9 on Qwen2-7B-Instruct and only 7.5 on AdvBench at a 0.05 ratio, and alignment-stage defenses slowed but did not stop the rise.
